policy.required_phrase: No canonical Minefield trap matches exactly. Possible unverified lead: <ID>.

leads.title: Persisted tool history can lose API-facing tool-result metadata
leads.symptom: Fresh structured tool calls work, but a resumed/persisted session later fails or behaves differently around prior tool results.
leads.possible_mechanism: Session persistence/replay may reconstruct role=tool history without required API-facing metadata even when internal tool identity survived.
leads.confirmation_check: Capture the fresh and resumed request histories; compare tool-result name, tool_call_id, assistant tool_calls object and ordering. Validate the repaired history with the same targeted validator.
leads.refutation_check: Show byte/field-equivalent tool history before and after persistence, or reproduce the failure with metadata intact.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Repair only the missing persisted-history metadata after the mismatch is observed; do not treat a one-turn tool smoke as persistence proof.

leads.title: Cold SM120 JIT can exhaust host memory after model load
leads.symptom: Startup dies during cold CUDA/FlashInfer compilation after large weights are already resident; it can look like an engine or GPU OOM.
leads.possible_mechanism: The host compiler process may compete with resident model weights for RAM and be OOM-killed.
leads.confirmation_check: Identify the killed PID/process and host OOM evidence; compare cold compile-after-load with prewarm-before-load on the same pinned build.
leads.refutation_check: Show the same cold compile succeeds with weights resident and no host pressure, or that the killed owner is the GPU engine rather than compiler.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Prewarm/version the JIT cache before model load and serialize heavy compile work, but only after host-compiler OOM is supported.

leads.title: Usable request admission can be lower than the advertised context/KV headline
leads.symptom: A request below configured/displayed context remains waiting before prefill without a normal OOM or immediate validation error.
leads.possible_mechanism: Whole-sequence block admission, reserved blocks and the live free-block pool may make a below-headline sequence unadmittable.
leads.confirmation_check: Record configured context, block size/count, reserved/free blocks and a pass/fail request-length boundary; confirm the request waits before prefill.
leads.refutation_check: Demonstrate admission up to the advertised boundary under the same block pool and scheduling state.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Reduce admitted request length/concurrency or change the qualified memory profile only after block arithmetic supports the diagnosis.
leads.notes: Qwen3.8 speculative-launch admission is a build/config-scoped extension: resource admission failure must not be generalized into a model-wide MTP unsupported claim.

leads.title: Benchmark selector can disagree with the backend actually measured
leads.symptom: The UI shows endpoint/model B selected but benchmark results still look like endpoint/model A.
leads.possible_mechanism: Control-plane selection may update display state while a proxy or request path continues routing to a default backend.
leads.confirmation_check: Use two mock backends with distinct model IDs/response markers and record the resolved request base in the benchmark receipt.
leads.refutation_check: Prove each selector choice reaches a distinct backend and receipt identity matches the selected target.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Route by the selected port/path and persist the resolved data-plane endpoint in every result.

leads.title: Stale injected skill/profile truth can override correct live configuration
leads.symptom: An agent answers with an old deployment/configuration even though the live provider config is correct.
leads.possible_mechanism: Retrieved/bootstrap/skill context shown to the model can be stale and contradict the control-plane configuration the harness actually uses.
leads.confirmation_check: Capture live provider config, exact model-facing injected context, and a bare-model control; show the stale fact exists in injected context and not the bare model.
leads.refutation_check: Show model-facing context contains the current truth or the stale answer occurs without stale injected material.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Fix the stale retrieval/bootstrap source and add a runtime truth receipt; do not blame the model before inspecting injected context.

leads.title: Accepted json_schema request may not mean the schema was enforced
leads.symptom: A response_format=json_schema request returns HTTP success and valid-looking JSON, but schema-specific constraints may not affect generation.
leads.possible_mechanism: The API path may accept the field while treating it as inert or applying only generic JSON-object constraints.
leads.confirmation_check: Use a deliberately restrictive schema that an unconstrained response predictably violates; compare accepted request and returned object against the exact schema.
leads.refutation_check: Show a schema-sensitive A/B where output changes to satisfy the supplied constraint and violations are rejected/prevented.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Validate output against the requested schema client-side until enforcement is demonstrated on the pinned server path.

leads.title: Bulk-copy bandwidth can hide many-small-copy loader bottlenecks
leads.symptom: Bulk H2D/D2D bandwidth looks healthy, but real model loading remains slow or rank-skewed.
leads.possible_mechanism: The production loader may issue many smaller transfers whose call-count/size geometry exposes overhead hidden by a bulk-copy microbenchmark.
leads.confirmation_check: Trace production copy sizes/counts per rank and compare with a microbenchmark reproducing that geometry.
leads.refutation_check: Show production copy geometry is bulk-like and throughput/skew matches the bulk benchmark.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Benchmark the transfer geometry the loader actually uses before changing storage/network assumptions.

leads.title: Cable/seating state can masquerade as cable-identity/EEPROM failure
leads.symptom: Cable/seating state may masquerade as cable-identity/EEPROM failure
leads.possible_mechanism: A physical seating/link-state problem may be misdiagnosed from identity/EEPROM symptoms.
leads.confirmation_check: Re-seat/change one physical path at a time and compare link/FEC/EEPROM state before replacing or reprogramming anything.
leads.refutation_check: Reproduce the fault with seating proven stable and show identity/EEPROM data itself changes or is invalid.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Treat reseat/link-state proof as the first reversible check.
leads.notes: Historical summary said MEASURED, later consolidation retained reproduction/sanitization gates; use as a lead until raw packet is reconciled.

leads.title: L2 MTU / PMTU mismatch can black-hole the high-speed path
leads.symptom: L2 MTU / PMTU mismatch may black-hole the high-speed path
leads.possible_mechanism: A host/switch MTU mismatch can pass small traffic while dropping larger packets or causing path-specific stalls.
leads.confirmation_check: Run size-stepped ping/PMTU and end-to-end jumbo tests across every relevant hop; inspect host MTU and switch L2 MTU together.
leads.refutation_check: Show the same large payloads pass end-to-end with the suspected MTU values unchanged.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Correct the smallest proven MTU/L2MTU mismatch; do not infer from link-up alone.
leads.notes: Historical summary said MEASURED, later consolidation retained reproduction/sanitization gates; use as a lead until raw packet is reconciled.

leads.title: TCP jumbo/MSS can fail while small or RDMA traffic still looks healthy
leads.symptom: TCP jumbo/MSS may fail while small or RDMA traffic still looks healthy
leads.possible_mechanism: Different transports/packet sizes can exercise different segmentation/path behavior, so a healthy small/RDMA probe does not prove jumbo TCP.
leads.confirmation_check: Run paired small TCP, jumbo TCP and RDMA tests on the same endpoints and inspect MSS/PMTU.
leads.refutation_check: Show jumbo TCP passes consistently under the same path state that was suspected.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Qualify each transport/size class separately before blaming the switch or NIC.
leads.notes: Historical summary said MEASURED, later consolidation retained reproduction/sanitization gates; use as a lead until raw packet is reconciled.

leads.title: Mixed distributed runtime/container images across ranks can mimic fabric failure
leads.symptom: Mixed distributed runtime/container images across ranks may mimic fabric failure
leads.possible_mechanism: Ranks using different images/builds may fail collectives or startup in ways that resemble networking faults.
leads.confirmation_check: Record immutable image digests/runtime versions on every rank and rerun with exact digest parity.
leads.refutation_check: Reproduce the failure with identical image digests and runtime libraries across all ranks.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Pin the same image digest and critical libraries across ranks before deeper network changes.
leads.notes: Historical summary said MEASURED, later consolidation retained reproduction/sanitization gates; use as a lead until raw packet is reconciled.

leads.title: Wrong HCA/interface selection can break an otherwise healthy distributed run
leads.symptom: Wrong HCA/interface selection may break an otherwise healthy distributed run
leads.possible_mechanism: A rank may bind to the wrong secondary NIC/HCA even though the intended high-speed interface is healthy.
leads.confirmation_check: Log selected HCA/interface/address per rank and compare to topology; force the known-good device only as a diagnostic A/B.
leads.refutation_check: Show the same failure with every rank bound to the intended HCA/interface.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Pin per-host HCA/interface selection after observing a mismatch.
leads.notes: Historical summary said MEASURED, later consolidation retained reproduction/sanitization gates; use as a lead until raw packet is reconciled.

leads.title: Out-of-band/default-route traffic can escape over the wrong network
leads.symptom: Out-of-band/default-route traffic may escape over the wrong network
leads.possible_mechanism: Control or compatibility traffic may follow Wi-Fi/default routing while data traffic uses the intended fabric, causing asymmetric or confusing failures.
leads.confirmation_check: Capture route lookup/source address for control and data destinations on each host; compare with socket/collective logs.
leads.refutation_check: Prove all relevant traffic uses the intended path while the failure persists.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Set explicit route/source-interface policy only after the escaped path is observed.
leads.notes: Historical summary said MEASURED, later consolidation retained reproduction/sanitization gates; use as a lead until raw packet is reconciled.

leads.title: Directional host-to-NIC/DMA impairment can be hidden by symmetric-looking tests
leads.symptom: Directional host-to-NIC/DMA impairment may be hidden by symmetric-looking tests
leads.possible_mechanism: One host is much slower when it is the writer/sender, while the same links and peers are fast in the opposite direction.
leads.confirmation_check: Run a directed all-pairs matrix and correlate speed with writer identity; add host-memory/NIC/DMA-local probes on the slow writer.
leads.refutation_check: Show direction-independent performance or move the bottleneck with the link/port rather than the writer host.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Investigate writer-side host memory, DMA, PCIe/IOMMU and NIC path before changing healthy switch topology.
leads.notes: Historical summary said MEASURED, later consolidation retained reproduction/sanitization gates; use as a lead until raw packet is reconciled.

leads.title: GPU tenancy/process ownership collision can mimic engine instability
leads.symptom: A second GPU process appears or reappears outside the expected service manager and the target serve becomes unstable or loses memory.
leads.possible_mechanism: Unexpected process ownership/tenancy may consume GPU or host resources independently of the target service.
leads.confirmation_check: Snapshot GPU/process ownership before and during failure; map every PID to service/session owner.
leads.refutation_check: Show no unexpected tenant exists while the same instability reproduces.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Remove/reconcile the unexpected tenant only after ownership is proven.

leads.title: GPU FP4 capability does not prove the runtime selected an FP4 backend
leads.symptom: Hardware advertises FP4/NVFP4 capability and checkpoint is labelled FP4, but performance/accuracy suggest a fallback or different kernel path.
leads.possible_mechanism: Hardware capability, checkpoint label and actual runtime quant/backend are separate facts.
leads.confirmation_check: Inspect loaded quant config, runtime logs/kernel/backend identity, and a path-specific probe.
leads.refutation_check: Show the intended backend/kernel actually executes for the relevant layers.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Report the effective backend and fix selection/config only after observing the mismatch.

leads.title: Native MTP can change memory/KV readiness even at K=1
leads.symptom: Baseline reaches READY but enabling native MTP K=1 changes the footprint enough that KV allocation fails at the same memory-utilization setting.
leads.possible_mechanism: Speculative configuration changes loaded/runtime memory and therefore invalidates the baseline memory qualification.
leads.confirmation_check: Compare READY footprint/KV allocation baseline vs MTP K=1 with identical non-spec settings; record actual free memory and KV blocks.
leads.refutation_check: Show equal footprint/readiness and KV allocation with and without MTP under the same settings.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Re-qualify memory utilization/KV settings for the speculative configuration; never publish a universal threshold.

leads.title: Session or automation lifetime can kill a healthy serve
leads.symptom: A server starts and works, then disappears when the launching shell/session/automation ends, looking like an engine crash.
leads.possible_mechanism: Process lifetime may be coupled to the control session rather than a durable service owner.
leads.confirmation_check: Track parent/cgroup/service ownership and timestamps around session exit; relaunch under a durable owner as a control.
leads.refutation_check: Show the process dies independently of session/control lifetime.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Use a durable process/service owner only after lifecycle coupling is proven.

leads.title: Forced capacity/block-count overrides do not create physical headroom
leads.symptom: A forced block/capacity value lets configuration pass but the runtime later stalls/OOMs or cannot admit work.
leads.possible_mechanism: Overriding a calculator can bypass a guard without changing physical memory available to weights, KV, graphs and runtime baseline.
leads.confirmation_check: Measure physical free memory and actual allocated blocks before/after the override and test admission/readiness.
leads.refutation_check: Show the forced value corresponds to physically allocatable memory with stable operation.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Remove the override or lower workload/capacity to the physically demonstrated envelope.

leads.title: Residual memory buckets need lifecycle attribution before blaming a subsystem
leads.symptom: Memory accounting leaves a large unexplained residual and one loader/runtime component is blamed by subtraction.
leads.possible_mechanism: Baseline runtime allocations before model load may own much of the residual; a numerical remainder is not causal attribution.
leads.confirmation_check: Take a lifecycle timeline: process baseline, post-runtime-init, post-model, post-KV/graphs, post-first-forward.
leads.refutation_check: Show the residual appears only when the suspected component is introduced and disappears when it is removed.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Do not tune/remove the suspected subsystem until the timeline localizes the allocation.

leads.title: Eager/debug launch flags can define the throughput regime
leads.symptom: Throughput is unexpectedly low while correctness looks fine, or two supposedly identical runs differ sharply.
leads.possible_mechanism: A correctness/debug flag can disable CUDA graphs or select eager execution, changing the benchmark regime.
leads.confirmation_check: Record graph/eager mode in runtime logs and run a matched A/B with only the launch flag changed.
leads.refutation_check: Show both arms use the same execution mode and performance difference persists.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Publish/compare results only with execution mode recorded; change the flag only after validating correctness.

leads.title: Operator-facing reasoning settings may differ from provider-bound settings
leads.symptom: A UI/profile says reasoning is on/off but the provider request does not reflect that setting or a different nested precedence wins.
leads.possible_mechanism: Profile nesting/precedence can make operator-facing configuration diverge from the actual request sent to the serving endpoint.
leads.confirmation_check: Capture the provider-bound request and relevant template/rendered fields for each arm.
leads.refutation_check: Show the intended setting is present and effective in the exact provider-bound request.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Base A/B labels on the provider-bound request, not UI/profile intent.

leads.title: Fail-closed tool containment is not successful tool-call reliability
leads.symptom: A guard safely refuses malformed native tool markup, but aggregate reporting treats the contained turn as a tool success.
leads.possible_mechanism: Safety containment and successful structured tool execution are different metrics.
leads.confirmation_check: Count malformed/refused turns separately from successfully parsed/executed tool calls.
leads.refutation_check: Show every contained turn also produced a valid structured call and successful execution.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Report containment rate and successful-call rate separately.

leads.title: Post-tool native-markup event was observed once but exact replay later stayed clean
leads.symptom: A historical post-tool turn emitted unexpected native markup, but a reconstructed exact replay later passed repeatedly.
leads.possible_mechanism: The original owner is unresolved; the event could depend on state not captured by the reconstruction.
leads.confirmation_check: Recover the exact original provider request/response and replay it on the pinned stack with surrounding session state.
leads.refutation_check: Repeated exact original replay stays clean and no missing state variable can be identified.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Do not apply a speculative fix; use the lead to avoid prematurely blaming the model or parser.

leads.title: Long-session garbling can persist after tool-history repair
leads.symptom: A long continuous session still produces occasional garbled turns after the known tool-history issue is repaired.
leads.possible_mechanism: Owner could be model, server, harness, desktop/session layer, or state accumulation; current evidence does not isolate it.
leads.confirmation_check: Reconstruct exact bad-turn provider requests/responses and replay them outside the long session, then with controlled accumulated state.
leads.refutation_check: Bad turns do not reproduce and all model-facing requests are shown equivalent to clean controls.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Preserve the bad-turn artifacts and avoid changing unrelated layers until replay localizes the owner.

leads.title: Client timeout can masquerade as benchmark/model failure
leads.symptom: Long-context or multi-turn benchmark items fail at the client timeout while the endpoint remains alive.
leads.possible_mechanism: The benchmark client may terminate before the server completes, turning a harness timeout into a model score failure.
leads.confirmation_check: Rerun only timed-out IDs with a deliberately generous explicit timeout and record server completion/status.
leads.refutation_check: Items still fail for the same semantic reason well before the generous timeout, or server itself fails.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Separate timeout from model-score failure and set a workload-appropriate explicit timeout.

leads.title: SM121 NVFP4 MoE can select the wrong CUTLASS path
leads.symptom: SM121 NVFP4 MoE runs but is wrong/unstable or performs unlike the expected path.
leads.possible_mechanism: A backend/kernel selection can choose an incompatible CUTLASS route where a Marlin path is required for the observed recipe.
leads.confirmation_check: Pin the historical source revision and inspect effective kernel/backend; run a small output-fidelity + performance A/B between candidate paths.
leads.refutation_check: Show the expected CUTLASS path is correct on the same build/model and output checks pass.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Force the known-good backend only after effective-path verification.
leads.notes: Static/public-repository lead from the pinned Keys/Inkling audit; not reproduced by Blackwellboy unless another source says so.

leads.title: `nvfp4` and `fp4_mx_block16` naming can identify different runtime expectations
leads.symptom: A supposedly NVFP4 path is rejected, misrouted, or silently uses a different implementation.
leads.possible_mechanism: Runtime dtype/quant identifiers may use a backend-specific name such as fp4_mx_block16 rather than a generic nvfp4 label.
leads.confirmation_check: Inspect accepted config enums and effective runtime path on the pinned build; compare both names in a no-model/static or tiny-path control.
leads.refutation_check: Both names resolve identically to the intended implementation.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Use the runtime's exact accepted/effective identifier and record it.
leads.notes: Static/public-repository lead from the pinned Keys/Inkling audit; not reproduced by Blackwellboy unless another source says so.

leads.title: Multiple KV writers can make one quantization hook incomplete
leads.symptom: KV looks correctly quantized on one path but other requests/steps show different memory or correctness behavior.
leads.possible_mechanism: More than one code path may write KV, including hidden-state/draft injection; patching only one writer leaves mixed representation.
leads.confirmation_check: Trace every writer into the target KV pool and assert representation/scale on each path.
leads.refutation_check: Prove all requests go through the one patched writer.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Quantize at the common pool/write boundary only after writer inventory is complete.
leads.notes: Static/public-repository lead from the pinned Keys/Inkling audit; not reproduced by Blackwellboy unless another source says so.

leads.title: Cap-accept can still pay full-width verification cost
leads.symptom: A speculative accept cap improves/controls acceptance statistics but throughput does not improve and may fall.
leads.possible_mechanism: Capping accepted tokens need not shrink the verifier's full-width work, so compute cost can remain while useful accepted output is truncated.
leads.confirmation_check: Profile verifier width/work and accepted-token count with cap on/off at matched prompts.
leads.refutation_check: Show verifier work shrinks in proportion to the cap and throughput responds accordingly.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Do not infer speedup from acceptance alone; tune only with matched throughput measurements.
leads.notes: Static/public-repository lead from the pinned Keys/Inkling audit; not reproduced by Blackwellboy unless another source says so.

leads.title: `/generate` prompt echo can corrupt a benchmark corpus
leads.symptom: Generated-output files include the prompt again, inflating token/text counts or breaking graders.
leads.possible_mechanism: An endpoint/client may return echoed prompt text that the benchmark treats as model completion.
leads.confirmation_check: Use a sentinel prompt and inspect raw response fields; compare completion-only extraction against stored corpus rows.
leads.refutation_check: Show stored outputs exclude the prompt byte-for-byte.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Strip only the documented echo field/prefix and retain raw response for audit.
leads.notes: Static/public-repository lead from the pinned Keys/Inkling audit; not reproduced by Blackwellboy unless another source says so.

leads.title: Stop-word ratio heuristics can falsely reject valid reasoning
leads.symptom: Reasoning outputs are marked bad or truncated by a stop-word ratio despite being semantically valid.
leads.possible_mechanism: A lexical stop-word heuristic can measure style/token distribution rather than reasoning validity.
leads.confirmation_check: Replay accepted/rejected rows with a semantic or task-grounded grader and inspect the exact stop-word calculation.
leads.refutation_check: Rejected rows are independently invalid and the heuristic has low false-positive rate on controls.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Treat the heuristic as an advisory feature, not a hard correctness gate, until calibrated.
leads.notes: Static/public-repository lead from the pinned Keys/Inkling audit; not reproduced by Blackwellboy unless another source says so.

leads.title: Speculative acceptance can be strongly temperature-dependent
leads.symptom: Acceptance changes sharply across runs that differ in sampling temperature, making a speculative speed comparison look like a kernel/runtime change.
leads.possible_mechanism: Sampling temperature changes target-token distribution and therefore draft/target agreement.
leads.confirmation_check: Run a temperature sweep with all runtime settings fixed and record acceptance + throughput distributions.
leads.refutation_check: Acceptance remains stable across the tested temperature range.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Match temperature before comparing speculative configurations.
leads.notes: Static/public-repository lead from the pinned Keys/Inkling audit; not reproduced by Blackwellboy unless another source says so.

leads.title: Temperature zero can still be nondeterministic; single-run peaks are weak evidence
leads.symptom: Repeated temp=0 runs produce different tokens/acceptance/speed, while a single peak is reported as representative.
leads.possible_mechanism: Runtime scheduling, kernels or tie-breaking can make nominal greedy runs non-bit-identical.
leads.confirmation_check: Repeat the exact request many times and report distribution/identity hashes, not only the maximum.
leads.refutation_check: Demonstrate byte-identical output and stable timings under repeated runs.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Use medians/distributions and preserve run count even at temp=0.
leads.notes: Static/public-repository lead from the pinned Keys/Inkling audit; not reproduced by Blackwellboy unless another source says so.

leads.title: Zero-shard calibration can be folded away under CUDA-graph/static execution
leads.symptom: A calibration/probe appears to pass while one shard/path effectively contributes zero work.
leads.possible_mechanism: Static graph/greedy folding can make a zero-shard path disappear from the measured execution.
leads.confirmation_check: Inject a nonzero sentinel per shard and verify each contributes to the captured graph/output.
leads.refutation_check: Show every shard is executed and contributes under the same captured graph.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Use per-shard sentinels and inspect the captured/static path before trusting aggregate calibration.
leads.notes: Static/public-repository lead from the pinned Keys/Inkling audit; not reproduced by Blackwellboy unless another source says so.

leads.title: Cap-accept can raise acceptance yet reduce throughput
leads.symptom: Acceptance metric improves after a cap/calibration change but end-to-end throughput drops.
leads.possible_mechanism: Acceptance percentage can improve while verification overhead, truncation or scheduling cost worsens useful throughput.
leads.confirmation_check: Matched A/B: acceptance, useful accepted tokens, verifier work, TTFT and tok/s across repeated prompts.
leads.refutation_check: Throughput improves consistently after controlling prompt/sampling/run order.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Optimize for end-to-end useful throughput, not acceptance percentage alone.
leads.notes: Static/public-repository lead from the pinned Keys/Inkling audit; not reproduced by Blackwellboy unless another source says so.

leads.title: Ragged verify `compact` default can be recipe/version-sensitive and crash the path
leads.symptom: A speculative serve crashes in the ragged/verification path when a launcher default is enabled.
leads.possible_mechanism: A launcher may default SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE=compact even where the documented recipe expects it unset and the compact path is not safe for the build.
leads.confirmation_check: Record effective env/default and run matched unset vs compact on the exact source revision with a minimal verification workload.
leads.refutation_check: Compact passes the same workload repeatedly on the pinned build.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Leave the mode unset/use the proven recipe only for the affected version; do not generalize across releases.
leads.notes: Static/public-repository lead from the pinned Keys/Inkling audit; not reproduced by Blackwellboy unless another source says so.

leads.title: Configured all-reduce fusion can be reported enabled after topology disables the effective path
leads.symptom: Logs/configuration say an all-reduce fusion is enabled, but the world-size/topology selects a different path or disables that optimization.
leads.possible_mechanism: Different allow-lists govern custom-allreduce and FlashInfer paths, while a later enabled-pass summary can reflect configuration fields rather than topology-effective state.
leads.confirmation_check: On the pinned build, choose a world size that differs across allow-lists; capture both disable/warning path and the later enabled summary; then inspect actual kernel path.
leads.refutation_check: Show the summary is topology-aware/effective-state-derived or both paths are actually enabled as reported.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Trust effective runtime-path evidence over an intent/config summary; record both when benchmarking.
leads.notes: Earlier 'silent odd-world-size fallback' framing was refuted/narrowed: warnings exist; the useful lead is configured-versus-effective reporting drift.

leads.title: Quiet-compliance classifiers can miss a degraded answer that still looks syntactically normal
leads.symptom: A model/harness produces plausible compliant-looking output while task capability has degraded, and a superficial classifier still passes it.
leads.possible_mechanism: A binary compliance classifier may not measure whether the substantive task was completed correctly.
leads.confirmation_check: Use task-grounded execution/reference grading on rows that the compliance classifier passes; measure false-pass rate.
leads.refutation_check: Classifier-passed rows independently meet task correctness at the required rate.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Do not use quiet-compliance as the sole capability metric.

leads.title: Judge capability floor can make an evaluator the bottleneck
leads.symptom: Scores plateau, invert or become noisy on difficult outputs even though stronger independent grading disagrees.
leads.possible_mechanism: The judge model may lack enough capability for the domain/task, so its preferences become the measurement ceiling.
leads.confirmation_check: Cross-grade the same frozen outputs with stronger/orthogonal judges and execution/verifiable checks where possible.
leads.refutation_check: Independent verifiable grading agrees with the original judge across hard cases.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Use a stronger or task-grounded grader when judge-floor evidence appears.

leads.title: Probe/control rows can contaminate the task denominator
leads.symptom: Benchmark accuracy changes because diagnostic/probe rows are counted as normal task rows.
leads.possible_mechanism: Mixed row types can be aggregated into one denominator even though probes are not scored tasks.
leads.confirmation_check: Enumerate row types and recompute metrics with task-only denominator; compare to published score.
leads.refutation_check: All denominator rows are documented scored tasks.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Separate probes/controls from scored task rows in schema and reporting.

leads.title: Kimi-K3 inline-system safety is source-inspected but still needs served-runtime verification
leads.symptom: A user needs to know whether a non-first system message remains a distinct role in a served Kimi-K3 prompt.
leads.possible_mechanism: Checkpoint Python encoder source has an explicit system-role branch, but trust_remote_code means the executed tokenizer comes from the pinned checkpoint and runtime behavior can drift with revision/loading path.
leads.confirmation_check: Serve the pinned Kimi-K3 revision with --trust-remote-code and inspect /tokenize for [user Q, system LATESYS, user Q2]; require a distinct system role segment.
leads.refutation_check: Rendered served prompt drops/welds the inline system message or executes different source than inspected.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Pin model revision/tokenizer class and verify served render before relying on inline-system semantics.

leads.title: Qwen3.8 MTP support can be runtime-build specific rather than model-wide
leads.symptom: A Qwen3.8-27B lane reports MTP unsupported, leading the operator to conclude the checkpoint or model family cannot use MTP.
leads.possible_mechanism: MTP capability can depend on the exact serving build, model-family support code and accepted speculative configuration; the same NVFP4 checkpoint was unsupported on one pinned runtime but passed a depth-1 canary on another.
leads.confirmation_check: Pin the exact image/build, inspect its Qwen-family MTP implementation and accepted configuration, then run the same bounded canary with MTP off and at depth 1.
leads.refutation_check: Show the same checkpoint and MTP configuration fails as unsupported across the compared runtimes after support code and launch semantics are verified equivalent.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Change runtime or speculative configuration only after localizing the unsupported boundary; do not describe one runtime result as a Qwen3.8 model limitation.
leads.notes: Aeon NVFP4 stage reported MTP_UNSUPPORTED; Drowzeys vLLM development image exposed Qwen-family MTP support and passed MTP1 on the same NVFP4 revision. Later depths were not claimed from the early checkpoint.

leads.title: amd64 benchmark images fail natively on arm64 DGX Spark before the model is tested
leads.symptom: A benchmark or helper container on DGX Spark dies immediately with exec format error and the run appears to be a model or benchmark failure.
leads.possible_mechanism: The benchmark image can be built for amd64 while the DGX Spark host is aarch64, so native execution fails before any request reaches the served model.
leads.confirmation_check: Record host architecture and inspect the architecture of every benchmark/helper image; reproduce the failure with a harmless container command before contacting the model endpoint.
leads.refutation_check: Show host and image architectures are compatible, the helper process starts normally, and the failure occurs only after a model request is actually sent.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Use a native arm64/multi-arch benchmark image or an explicitly qualified emulation path; do not score the model from a pre-endpoint exec-format failure.
leads.notes: Observed with an amd64 task_cleanroom_v6 image on an aarch64 Spark host; native run returned exec format error and the campaign held the benchmark.

leads.title: Docker save/load can preserve runtime content while the local image ID differs from the source repo digest
leads.symptom: A transferred serving image is rejected as the wrong build because its local Docker .Id does not equal the registry digest pinned before docker save/load.
leads.possible_mechanism: A registry RepoDigest identifies a registry manifest while Docker .Id identifies the image configuration; comparing those different digest classes is not a valid equality test. After transfer, experiment provenance still requires the complete executable image configuration and ordered filesystem identity to match the intended source.
leads.confirmation_check: Preserve the source registry RepoDigest and, before transfer when possible, the source image .Id/config digest. After load, compare the complete image configuration JSON or config digest (including Entrypoint, Cmd, User, WorkingDir and environment) plus ordered RootFS/layer identity and architecture. Do not accept a subset of labels/environment fields as full image equivalence.
leads.refutation_check: Show the source and loaded complete image configuration or config digest differs, any ordered RootFS/layer identity differs, architecture differs, or the transferred image executes a different entrypoint/command path.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Do not require Docker .Id to equal a registry RepoDigest. Instead compare like-for-like identities: registry manifest provenance separately, and complete source-vs-loaded image configuration plus ordered filesystem identity for execution equivalence.
leads.notes: The campaign correctly rejected LOCAL_ID == source RepoDigest as an identity predicate and initially used a 46-layer fingerprint plus selected config labels. This public Minefield lead strengthens the reusable check: selected config fields are insufficient; compare the complete executable image configuration (or its config digest/pre-transfer image ID) as well as ordered filesystem identity.

leads.title: Container ENTRYPOINT can reinterpret a model path as a CLI subcommand
leads.symptom: A vLLM-derived container exits before model load with 'Usage: serve ...' and 'No such command /model'.
leads.possible_mechanism: The image ENTRYPOINT already invokes a serve CLI whose argv contract differs from the launcher assumption, so appending /model places the model path in a subcommand position.
leads.confirmation_check: Inspect Docker Entrypoint and Cmd, run the image help path, and record the exact final argv; compare with a corrected invocation that reaches a bounded model canary.
leads.refutation_check: Show the final argv matches the image CLI contract and the same No-such-command failure persists after the model path is passed in the documented position.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Adapt the launcher to the image entrypoint contract rather than changing weights or runtime support code.
leads.notes: The same pinned image/checkpoint later returned BLACKWELL38_READY after launch construction was corrected. A separate truendocker shell-concatenation typo is not merged into this mechanism.

leads.title: A telemetry Thread._stop name collision can crash a soak worker at teardown while the endpoint remains healthy
leads.symptom: A long model soak serves requests, then the worker crashes during thread join/teardown and the run is mistaken for serving instability.
leads.possible_mechanism: A threading.Thread subclass can shadow the inherited private _stop() method by assigning a threading.Event to self._stop; Thread.join later attempts to call the Event as a method.
leads.confirmation_check: Inspect the worker traceback and Thread subclass fields; preserve request/server telemetry separately; rename the field and rerun an offline join regression plus the bounded soak.
leads.refutation_check: Show the server itself restarted/died or requests failed before harness teardown, or reproduce the worker crash without any Thread private-name collision.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Fix the harness lifecycle bug and rerun; do not change model/runtime configuration on the basis of a teardown-only worker exception.
leads.notes: After _stop was renamed to _stop_event, the recovered Qwen3.8 BF16 Spark soak completed about two hours with 512/512 successful requests and zero server restarts.

leads.title: One Qwen3.8 Q4 decimal canary failure did not reproduce on the immediate pinned rerun
leads.symptom: A simple decimal-comparison canary on a Qwen3.8 Q4_K_M llama.cpp lane returns the wrong number once and is immediately labelled quantization corruption.
leads.possible_mechanism: The bad response is real but a single response does not localize cause; sampling/defaults, runtime variance, prompt path or quantization remain competing explanations when the immediate pinned rerun passes.
leads.confirmation_check: Capture the exact provider-bound request, effective sampling/defaults and raw output, then repeat the same canary across enough runs and compare a higher-precision or otherwise controlled arm.
leads.refutation_check: If repeated exact requests stay clean and no quant-specific A/B localizes the failure, refute the quant-corruption causal label while retaining the original bad response as an observation.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Do not change the quant or checkpoint from n=1; first make the failure repeatable and localize it with a controlled arm.
leads.notes: Pinned campaign first returned 9.11 on the decimal canary and held; the immediate rerun returned 9.9 and passed. Cause was not isolated.

leads.title: Requested NVFP4 backend can differ from the effective kernel on SM121
leads.symptom: A GB10/SM121 NVFP4 serve is incoherent under one backend setting and coherent after requesting another backend, but configuration intent alone does not prove which kernel actually ran.
leads.possible_mechanism: Backend-selection controls may be build/version specific or ignored, so a requested Marlin-versus-default A/B can accidentally compare the same effective kernel or attribute a build-scoped correctness difference too broadly.
leads.confirmation_check: Pin the exact image/build and model revision, prove the effective kernel/backend from runtime evidence on both arms, then run identical correctness canaries before comparing speed or coherence.
leads.refutation_check: Show the requested controls are recognized, both arms use the intended distinct effective backends, and the reported coherence difference does not reproduce under the same checkpoint/request.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Do not force or recommend a backend from flag names alone; use only a backend path whose effective kernel and correctness are proven on the pinned build.
leads.notes: The public-source coherence claim remains unreproduced here. A separate first-party Qwen3.8 check found requested Marlin controls unrecognized on its tested build, sharpening the required requested-versus-effective-backend check without reproducing the external result.

leads.title: Sampler-enforced thinking budgets can bound Qwen3.8 reasoning without redefining the effort prompt
leads.symptom: Qwen3.8 at a high reasoning-effort setting can consume the entire completion budget inside thinking and return empty final content, while prompt-only effort labels provide no hard reasoning-token ceiling.
leads.possible_mechanism: vLLM 0.27.1 exposes thinking_token_budget and implements sampler-side tracking that forces the configured end-of-thinking token sequence when the budget is exhausted; this separates an engine-enforced reasoning budget from prompt wording such as xhigh.
leads.confirmation_check: On one pinned Qwen3.8 checkpoint/runtime, hold explicit reasoning_effort, max completion tokens, sampling and prompt constant; compare no budget versus a fixed thinking_token_budget while recording rendered prompt, reasoning/content token counts, finish reason, correctness and latency.
leads.refutation_check: Show the exact vLLM build lacks the budget path, the request does not reach it, or a matched budget-vs-no-budget A/B fails to change the reasoning-limit behavior despite the sampler control being active.
leads.conditional_mitigation: Where the pinned vLLM build and reasoning parser support it, prefer an explicitly measured sampler-side thinking budget over relying on an unbounded xhigh prompt instruction; do not retrofit the setting into historical benchmark arms.
leads.notes: Implementation existence is source-confirmed in vLLM 0.27.1. The reported Qwen3.8 GB10 numeric A/B (no budget: 97,708 reasoning chars / 0 content; budget 1500: 5,562 reasoning chars / 18,512 content) remains external contributor measurement and has not been reproduced by Blackwellboy.
